question: According to the first National Multidimensional Poverty Index by NITI Aayog, which state has the maximum percentage of poor people?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **first National Multidimensional Poverty Index** by NITI Aayog,** Bihar **has the maximum percentage of** poor people.**
 
• Bihar has a poverty rate of **33.7%**, which is the **highest **among all Indian states.
 
• The National Multidimensional Poverty Index takes into account various factors such as** education, health, and living standards** to measure poverty.
 
• The index helps policymakers identify the most deprived regions and take** targeted actions** to improve their living conditions.
 
• Other states in the options are also known for their **poverty levels.**
 
• For instance, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh have poverty rates o**f 26.1% and 29.4%** respectively, while Jharkhand has a poverty rate of **28.8%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Madhya Pradesh:** The state has a **large tribal population** and is known for its** high poverty levels,** particularly in rural areas.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh: **The state has a large population and is one of the** most populous states** in India.
 
 
• **Poverty** is a major issue in both rural and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Jharkhand:** The state has a high poverty rate due to a combination of factors such as** low literacy levels, inadequate healthcare facilities, and lack of infrastructure. **
 
• **Bihar: **The state has the** highest poverty rate** in India, with a large population living **below the poverty line.**
 
 
• The state government has launched several initiatives to** address poverty **and improve the **living conditions** of the poor.
